clue.text: Somebody's behind such a forward-looking form of advertisement

definitions.text: Somebody's behind such a forward-looking form of advertisement

parts.words: Somebody's behind such a forward-looking form of advertisement
parts.note: a man carrying a pair of placards hung over his shoulders has one at his back and one at his front, so his behind is covered by such an advert while the other faces forward

explanation.surface: A remark that someone is backing a progressive kind of advertising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' reads as 'supporting' and 'forward-looking' as 'progressive', but both are literal: the board hangs at the wearer's back and front.
explanation.definitionFit: Two hinged placards worn front and back by a walking advertiser form exactly this sort of advert.

clue.text: Actions Indy arranged for sharing with other papers

indicators.note: arranged says the letters of the two words before it are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written; the nickname of the Independent newspaper

explanation.surface: Stories from the Independent are reworked for distribution to rival newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: Selling the same column or feature to several publications at once is the newspaper practice in question.

clue.text: Human being changed into prophet

indicators.note: changed signals that the letters of the word Human are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mere mortal is transformed into a seer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Human being' looks like one phrase, but only 'Human' is fodder; 'being changed into' links it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: He is one of the twelve minor prophets of the Old Testament, with a book under his name.

clue.text: Philosophy of life only an astronaut can have?

definitions.text: Philosophy of life only an astronaut can have?

parts.words: Philosophy of life only an astronaut can have?
parts.note: read literally, a view of the whole planet from space is something only a space traveller could get, while the phrase normally means an outlook on life

explanation.surface: A wry question about what outlook belongs only to space travellers.
explanation.definitionFit: The compound means a comprehensive personal outlook or philosophy, and literally a sight of the globe.

clue.text: Belligerent Russian taking officer's BE wine

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for commanding officer, with the possessive S
sack is an old name for a dry white fortified wine such as sherry

explanation.surface: A warlike Russian helps himself to his commander's wine.
explanation.walkthrough: SACK is the sherry-type wine drunk in Shakespeare's day (Falstaff's favourite). The 'BE' in the clue as held appears to be stray print and plays no part.
explanation.definitionFit: These horsemen of the Russian steppes were famed as fierce soldiers, so a warlike Russian fits.

clue.text: Later in text, American author appears half-hearted

indicators.note: half-hearted says one of the pair of letters at the centre of the name is dropped

parts.note: Saul Bellow was a Nobel-winning American novelist

explanation.surface: Further on in a book, a US writer turns out lukewarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-hearted' removes one of the two central Ls from BELLOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Writers say 'see below' to point to something further down or later in a document.

clue.text: Fog later dispersed, with some residual light

indicators.note: dispersed says the letters of fog and later are scattered and regrouped

explanation.surface: Once the mist has lifted, a little light lingers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dispersed' turns FOG LATER into AFTERGLO; W for 'with' completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: The glow left in the sky after sunset, or after any light source fades, is leftover light.

clue.text: Musicians performing, one by one

definitions.meaning: a pair of players performing together
read literally, one alongside another one makes two

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a pair of performers, and one beside one is a pair.

clue.text: A very little piece of plain chocolate

indicators.note: piece of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Asking for just a small square of dark chocolate.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatically, giving 'an inch' means yielding a tiny amount, so a very little.

clue.text: Degree of detail in sorting out of problem

definitions.meaning: the sharpness of an image or screen, measured in pixels
the settling or solving of a difficulty

explanation.surface: How much precision goes into fixing a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both image sharpness and the act of settling a difficulty.

clue.text: How to publicise moderate policy

definitions.meaning: read literally as Latin-English, by way of the press and broadcasters

explanation.surface: Advice on promoting a middle-of-the-road political line.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means a middle way, and literally 'by way of the media'.

clue.text: Lacked experience on return to European city

indicators.note: on return says the phrase is read backwards

parts.note: was raw: a raw recruit lacks experience

explanation.surface: A green traveller comes back to a European capital.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the capital of Poland, a city in central Europe.

clue.text: Explosives expert as head in new federal lab, initially

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
new signals that the letters of federal are made anew in another order

parts.note: nob is slang for the head

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of lab

explanation.surface: A bomb-maker leading a fresh government laboratory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges the letters of 'federal' into ALFREDE, and 'in' sets the head slang inside it, ahead of the final E. 'as' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swedish chemist invented dynamite, so he was an expert in explosives.

clue.text: Carefully selected, as flowers usually are

definitions.meaning: literally, blooms are generally gathered by hand

explanation.surface: Chosen with care, like most flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means chosen with care, and literally gathered by hand.

clue.text: Champ among boxers, for example, in Check tod ruthless competition

indicators.note: among puts one word inside the other

parts.note: boxers are a breed of dog, so more than one gives two dogs
to champ is to chew, or eat

explanation.surface: A title-holder among fighters in a cut-throat contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champ' looks like a champion but is the verb, to munch; 'among' puts EAT between the two DOGs. 'in Check tod' in the clue as held appears to be stray print.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a contest where everyone will harm others to succeed.

clue.text: Split in political group

definitions.meaning: the socialist or radical wing of politics

explanation.surface: A rift in a party.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means departed (past tense of leave) and the radical wing of politics.

clue.text: VIP initially unable to move

definitions.meaning: a very important person, such as a monarch
in chess this piece is hemmed in at the start of the game

explanation.surface: A celebrity who cannot get going at first.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch is the ultimate VIP, and the chess piece of that name is blocked in at the start.

clue.text: Navigation aid composer used, going over hilltops

indicators.note: going over says the composer's name surrounds the hilltops

parts.note: Carl Maria von Weber was a German composer
the brow of a hill is its top

explanation.surface: A composer found his way using a guide over the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going over' means the composer's name straddles the hilltops. 'used' is only a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Software for moving between internet pages helps you navigate the web.

clue.text: Bill hunted them down in New York, city

definitions.meaning: the bison, which ... Bill Cody hunted
a city in New York State

explanation.surface: A Wild West hunter pursues his quarry to New York.
explanation.definitionFit: The animal Buffalo Bill shot and a city in upstate New York share the name.

clue.text: Analyse a French rugby, unit

parts.note: un is French for a
the forwards in rugby are called the pack

explanation.surface: Breaking down a French rugby squad.
explanation.walkthrough: The PACK is the group of forwards in a rugby team.
explanation.definitionFit: To unpack an argument is to examine it in detail, as when unloading a case.

clue.text: Opener bagging runs repeatedly for county

indicators.note: bagging means holding inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: a key opens a lock

indicators.note: repeatedly says the letter is given twice

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cricket opening batsman piling up runs for his county side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opener' looks like a cricket opening batsman, but here it means something that opens a lock. 'bagging' means holding the doubled runs inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a county in south-west Ireland.

clue.text: Female commander manipulating meeting at one point

parts.note: OC stands for officer commanding
using someone means manipulating them

explanation.surface: A woman officer pulling strings at a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Rays of light converging to a single point are said to be coming to a focus.

clue.text: City given another name when burnt

definitions.text: City given another name when burnt

parts.words: City given another name when burnt
parts.note: an Italian city whose name, prefixed by 'burnt', becomes the name of a reddish-brown pigment

explanation.surface: A town renamed after being torched.
explanation.walkthrough: Burnt sienna is an artist's earth pigment named after the Tuscan city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tuscan city lends its name to a pigment that becomes another colour when roasted.

clue.text: Blunter euphemism for nonsense!

parts.note: balder means plainer, blunter
dash is a polite stand-in for damn

explanation.surface: A cry that 'nonsense' is a polite word for something stronger.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a synonym for drivel or empty talk.

clue.text: Music broadcast

definitions.meaning: to put out on radio or television

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a tune and also to transmit a programme.

clue.text: What can be accomplished back in place of exile

indicators.note: back says the word is read in reverse

parts.note: able, in the sense of capable of being done

explanation.surface: Finding out what can be done once returned to banishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon was banished to this Mediterranean island in 1814.

clue.text: Its goals include conversions (5,8) 23,424 Solutio

parts.note: in this oval-ball game a conversion is a kick at goal after a try, though the surface suggests religious or financial conversions

explanation.surface: A movement whose aims include winning converts.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue as held ends with stray print from the page ('23,424 Solutio'), which plays no part.
explanation.definitionFit: Converting a try by kicking over the posts is part of scoring in this code of football.
